I guessed all qtl are significant based on Chi2 and F value, is it
collect?
some people asked me some of the qtl which has low LOD (such as 4.5,
chr27) may not be significant because my individual number is very low
(n=125). the result of permutation test using scanone was 3.49
alpha=0.05, even though that value is hard to be applied to MIM.

Second is 1.5 lod interval.
I read some papers which use 1.5 lod interval as a 95% confident
interval, but all of them I read use single qtl model (=scanone). is
it possible to apply MIM to see the confident interval? or would you
tell me way which is better to be applied to MIM?

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] significance of detected QTL and lod interval of fitqtl
parts:
I'm unfortunately not really able to answer either of your questions.

Regarding assessing significance of QTL in the output of fitqtl, you
don't want to take
the p-values at face value, as you need to take account of the scan
for loci. I do think
that the application of the permutation threshold you get from a one-
dimensional scan will
be reasonable, but this has not been well proven.

Regarding confidence intervals for QTL location in the context of a
multiple-QTL model,
this has not been well studied. Probably 1.5-LOD support intervals
are not too bad. Ideally,
these would be calculated taking into account the uncertainty of the
locations of other QTL,
but this would be quite difficult to calculate. I think what has
usually been done is to
consider the profile LOD curve of each QTL, keeping the positions of
all other QTL fixed
at their estimated locations.

karl
